code: extern "C" int LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput(const uint8_t *Data, size_t Size) {
note: The raw PoC bytes enter the libFuzzer harness as Data with byte length Size.
The harness creates a malloc-backed IO descriptor whose backing allocation is exactly the fuzzer input size.
The PoC bytes are copied into the malloc:// descriptor that later services binary parser reads.
The harness opens binary analysis on the same descriptor, causing radare2 to identify the PoC as Mach-O and prepare bin metadata.
The ia command requests all binary info, including Mach-O sections and metadata, which drives additional reads through the IO-backed RBuffer.
The binary loader represents the opened malloc:// descriptor as an RBuffer backed by RIO callbacks instead of a private byte array.
Parser reads from the RBuffer are forwarded with their requested length to the IO descriptor read callback.
The requested RBuffer read length is passed unchanged to descriptor-level IO.
Descriptor reads forward the same count to the active IO plugin after permission checks.
Because the descriptor is malloc://, the plugin read dispatch reaches io_memory_read with the caller supplied stack buffer and length.
io_memory_read initializes count bytes before clamping count to the remaining malloc:// backing size, so an oversized parser read can write past a smaller caller stack buffer.
After the late clamp, the function copies attacker-controlled Mach-O bytes from the malloc:// backing store into the same stack destination, completing the crashing write path.
